summary: On-demand export of 'transactional_activity' ledger as segmented NDJSON with per-tenant resume tokens and field-translation lexicon
description:
Issue summary:
North Harbor Bank has requested an on-demand export of the transactional_activity audit ledger for a legal review. They require a segmented NDJSON export that includes: per-tenant resume tokens per segment, canonical UTC anchoring for all timestamps, and a field-name translation lexicon (customer -> bank field names) so downstream forensic tools map correctly. Export must preserve ordering within tenant sequences and include a small manifest with segment checksums for reproducibility.

Impact:
- Customer cannot produce a legally-scoped playback for a compliance request without this export.
- High priority due to pending regulatory deadline in customer legal team.

Environment:
- Production activity ledger (prod - us-east).
- Primary ingestion path: webhook -> kafka -> ledger service -> archival exporter.

Steps to reproduce / request template used by customer:
1) Customer sent request via the Console "On-demand audit export" modal requesting: stream=transactional_activity, date_range=2025-10-01..2025-10-15, tenant_scope=tenant_9853, output_format=ndjson_segmented, include_resume_tokens=true, timestamp_mode=utc_canonical, include_field_lexicon=true, delivery=presigned_s3.
2) Support confirmed receipt and escalated to export ops.

Observed data / logs:
- Initial validation run (2025-11-03 14:05 UTC) showed ~0.4% of tenant events had sequence gaps.
- Ledger exporter logs: exporter/segment_writer WARN shard-lag detected on shard-7 between 2025-10-08T02:10:05Z and 2025-10-08T02:12:30Z.
- Kafka consumer offsets showed transient rebalances during the requested window.
- No authentication errors; S3 presigned write succeeded in dry-run.

Requested deliverable (customer acceptance):
- One or more NDJSON files partitioned by tenant sequence ranges (max 1M events / segment).
- A manifest.json (small) listing segments, per-segment SHA256 checksum, inclusive timestamp range, and a resume_token representing a stable offset for that tenant range.
- A CSV field-translation lexicon mapping Redwood field names -> North Harbor canonical field names.
- All timestamps in UTC ISO8601 with explicit tz (e.g. 2025-10-01T00:00:00Z).
- Delivery via presigned S3 URL with 7-day validity and a signed delivery receipt.

Acceptance criteria:
- Customer can replay the segments in-order without gaps using the resume tokens and manifest.
- Field mappings applied by customer result in no loss of critical attributes used by their compliance tooling.
- CRC/SHA checksums match on both sides.

Investigation notes (internal):
- Hypothesis A: kafka rebalances led to duplicate offset commits causing perceived sequence gaps for tenant_9853 only (tenant has high event density).
- Hypothesis B: temporary exporter shard-lag caused exporter to flush partial segments and then resume with new segment IDs, leaving apparent gaps until remapped by resume token logic.
- Action taken: replayed offset window to a staging export to verify segment continuity (INT-3321). Staging export produced contiguous segments but with different resume tokens than production run.
- Mitigation: we can stitch contiguous segments together in the exported manifest and provide synthetic resume tokens that map to per-segment start offsets for customer playback. Need SRE sign-off for token mutation approach.

Risks / compliance notes:
- Resume tokens are considered sensitive because they implicitly reveal offset state; shared tokens must be treated as limited-scope and delivered via secure presigned S3.
- Legalhold: customer requested preservation flags to avoid deletion; follow-up required with retention team.

Next steps / work items:
- [Support] Confirm final date window and whether additional tenant IDs included (Samantha - 2025-11-03).
- [SRE] Produce a curated NDJSON export from a controlled replay with stitched manifest (Marco - target 2025-11-06).
- [Export Ops] Generate CSV field lexicon based on customer-supplied mapping file and our schema (Nora - target 2025-11-06).
- [Security] Approve presigned S3 parameters and delivery receipt format (Ajay - target 2025-11-05).

Deliverables timeline: tentative - curated export available 2025-11-06 for customer review.
comments: 2025-11-03 - Samantha Lee (Support): Received initial request and validated required parameters. Asked customer for confirmation on tenant scope and retention hold flag.
2025-11-03 - Customer (North Harbor Legal - Maria Chen): Confirmed tenant_9853 only. Requested retention hold for exported slices and asked for checkable integrity proof for court submission.

2025-11-04 - Marco Ruiz (SRE): Investigated exporter logs. Found shard-lag on shard-7 during 2025-10-08; kafka consumer group had two rebalances. Starting a controlled replay to generate curated segments.
2025-11-04 - Ajay Patel (Security): Presigned S3 delivery OK with 7-day expiry; recommend using AES-GCM per-object encryption metadata and one-time retrieval link in support channel.
2025-11-05 - Nora Kim (Export Ops): Field lexicon draft uploaded to internal drive and linked in Confluence page. Waiting on legalhold flag from customer to apply preservation metadata to objects.
2025-11-06 - Samantha Lee (Support): Curated export uploaded to staging S3. Sent presigned URL to customer for verification and asked for confirmation on manifest/resume token format acceptance.
notes_for_engineering: If SRE cannot produce native resume tokens that are stable, implement translation layer that maps exporter offsets -> synthetic stable tokens and include mapping in manifest. Ensure mapping is cryptographically anchored (HMAC) and documented in manifest schema.
customer_communication_log: All customer-sensitive items delivered via secured presigned S3 link and support email. Legal hold confirmation pending.
